This week, Representative Darren Soto and I introduced the “Federal Investment Restrictions on Equipment from Worrisome Authoritarian Linked Locations (FIREWALL) Act. This bipartisan legislation is designed to safeguard America's telecommunications infrastructure from foreign adversaries by prohibiting federal telecommunications funding from being used to purchase fiber-optic cable sourced from countries of concern. The legislation builds upon ongoing efforts to secure U.S. communications networks from foreign threats and prevent hostile regimes from gaining access to critical American infrastructure. America's telecommunications networks are the backbone of our economy, our national security, and our daily lives. As our adversaries become increasingly sophisticated in their efforts to infiltrate critical infrastructure, we must act proactively to protect our communications systems from potential vulnerabilities. The FIREWALL Actensures that taxpayer dollars are not used to subsidize technology sourced from countries that pose a threat to our national security. Rather than waiting until these products are deeply embedded in our networks and facing another costly 'rip and replace' effort, we should take commonsense steps now to prevent the problem from occurring in the first place.

B000490.text: This week, the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, appeared before the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government. During the hearing, I asked the Director about how Congress can be any clearer to ensure that the Trump Administration understands that once a funding bill is signed into law, the President is not allowed to change or second-guess the spending and withhold it due to policy or political differences. That is at the heart of Article 1 of the U.S. Constitution and why Congress also passed the Impoundment Control Act of 1974, when President Nixon tried to withhold funds that were already obligated according to the law.

This week, I asked the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, to explain how poorly planned cuts to the federal workforce last year have weakened services and protections upon which Americans rely. This includes the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, which is responsible for protecting America’s agriculture from invasive species and diseases. USDA-APHIS began mounting a vigorous response to the resurgence of New World Screwworm – a deadly parasite affecting livestock – in 2024. However, in early 2025, the Administration illegally fired workers and forced others to resign, causing over 25 percent of all USDA-APHIS employees to leave. USDA’s New World Screwworm prevention, monitoring, surveillance, and control efforts were halted. Terrorists. Cartels. Human traffickers. Drug smugglers. Each day, ICE and Border Patrol agents and officers confront these threats head-on to keep America safe. It’s exactly why I have consistently voted to comprehensively resource these law enforcement professionals as they carry out their security missions. While the far-left hoped to eradicate funding for critical operations and weaken our border security apparatus, House Republicans have made clear that we will continue to support those who defend our homeland and keep our communities safe. That's why we passed the Secure America Act today. However, while I do not regret the objective of our actions today, I am appalled by the complete failure of Senate Democrats that led us to this moment. Chuck Schumer and his radical caucus twice shut down the government, instigating chaos across the nation. Since then, they have continued to diminish Article I and forced the use of reconciliation. It’s wrong – and deliberately undermines the appropriations process. The Constitution entrusts Congress with the power of the purse. Yet, in great irony, the Senate has shown greater concern for protecting an internal rule than fulfilling its constitutional duty. The filibuster is nothing more than an institutional habit. It is neither mentioned nor sanctioned in our founding documents. I would remind my peers on the other side of the Rotunda that no chamber precedent is greater than the bedrock of our Republic. Members swear an oath to uphold the Constitution – not the filibuster. I thoroughly regret the erosion of Article I authority that Senate Democrats have instigated, and the price everyday Americans have been forced to pay as a result. I hope the months-long charade that led us to this moment serves as a reminder that no partisan fixation is worth shutting down the government, abandoning constitutional responsibilities, and forcing Congress into extraordinary measures simply to perform its most basic duties. I believe in the Constitution, the power of the purse, and completing the appropriations process. I also believe in keeping the homeland safe. The Senate may have abandoned proper governing, but I will not abandon those who stand watch over our borders and protect our communities. Our work, of course, doesn’t end here. As the Fiscal Year 2027 Appropriations markups near completion, I am reminded that governing is a choice. The work I do, the votes I cast, and the actions I take will always be guided by one principle: fulfilling our obligations to the American people

Today, our nation celebrates 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence. 250 years ago, our nation overthrew the autocratic rule of King George III, defining our nation’s identity. On Independence Day and every day, I’m grateful for our servicemembers, military families, and veterans who bravely defend our freedom. From the Fundamental Orders of Connecticut, the first written constitution in the colonies, to Governor Jonathan Trumbull’s steadfast support for the Revolutionary cause, our state played an outsized role in the fight for independence. Connecticut earned the nickname “The Provision State” by supplying the Continental Army with food and materials that sustained the fight for freedom. The people of eastern Connecticut were right at the forefront of the Revolution- military leaders such as Major General Israel Putnam of Brooklyn Connecticut, as well as Governor Jonathan Trumbull of Lebanon, the only Colonial Governor to support the rebellion against England. The spirit of service remains part of who we are. Eastern Connecticut continues to strengthen our nation through military service, manufacturing, shipbuilding, agriculture, and so much more. On America’s 250th birthday, we can take pride in the role that our region has played in our nation’s past and continues to play in its future.

C001063.text: This afternoon, while in Duval County alongside County Judge Arnold Cantu, County Sheriff Romeo Ramirez, County Clerk Sally Lichtenberger, and the Commissioners' Court, I announced $170,000 in federal funding I secured through the FY2025 Operation Stonegarden Grant Program for the Duval County Sheriff's Office. I helped create Operation Stonegarden because I knew our border communities needed a reliable federal partnership to support local law enforcement. Since Duval County joined the program in 2018, it has received more than $1.4 million to help cover personnel, equipment, supplies, and other operational costs. These federal dollars will help fund overtime for deputies, expand law enforcement coverage, strengthen public safety across Duval County, and ensure local officers have the resources they need to continue protecting our communities.

Today, alongside Zapata County Judge Joe Rathmell, Justice of the Peace Olga Bruni, Zapata County Sheriff Ramon Montes, and Commissioner Joey Solis, I announced $293,070 in federal funding I secured through the FY2025 Operation Stonegarden Grant Program for the Zapata County Sheriff's Office. As the original author of Operation Stonegarden, I've continued fighting to ensure our border communities have the resources they need to keep families safe. Since the program's creation, Zapata County has received more than $10.3 million through Operation Stonegarden to support local law enforcement. This funding will support overtime for local deputies, strengthen law enforcement efforts, enhance public safety across Zapata County, and allow the Sheriff's Office to purchase brand-new patrol units, helping improve emergency response capabilities throughout the county.

This morning, I announced $25 million in federal dollars I secured through the U.S. Department of Transportation's BUILD Grant Program for the City of Laredo's World Trade Bridge Expansion Project. This investment will help add two new lanes to the existing bridge and construct a new eight-lane northbound commercial bridge, increasing capacity, reducing congestion, and keeping goods moving more efficiently through our nation's busiest commercial port of entry. Today's announcement builds on my continued efforts to secure federal investments for Laredo's international bridges. In addition to this $25 million BUILD Grant, I've helped secure a $62 million renovation project for Bridge II and a $27 million renovation project for Bridge I in 2015, ensuring our ports of entry remain competitive and prepared for continued growth. Thank you to Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño, the City of Laredo, and all of our partners who helped make this project possible. I'll continue working to bring federal investments home and ensure South Texas has the infrastructure it needs to support jobs, strengthen our supply chain, and keep American trade moving. Together, we're continuing to strengthen Laredo's position as the nation's #1 inland port.

For 250 years, our great experiment has faltered, flourished, evolved, and progressed. The American experience is ever-changing and as diverse as the people who call this country home. But one thing has remained constant – the idea of America has always been a beacon of hope. Protecting this country and the ideals and values it was founded on takes work. Democracy is demanding. It takes dedication and principle. And it takes the resounding belief that upholding those ideals and values is worth the fight because America is bigger than any one person. Because liberty can only truly endure when it is paired with responsibility, virtue, and a commitment to put public good ahead of personal ambition. Today, we celebrate the moment when our founding fathers openly declared that creating this country, based in liberty, was a necessity in the face of tyranny. Their legacy is that leadership requires courage when it’s difficult, integrity when no one is watching, and a willingness to put country above self. We must remember that our duty is not merely to the next election, but to the next generation. That should be the challenge for all Americans as we look forward to another 250 years. From Massachusetts, where the fight for freedom first began, I wish you a happy 4th of July. God Bless America always, God Bless all who call her home, and God Bless our courageous men and women in uniform who continue the fight for liberty today.

On Monday, our office suffered an unimaginable loss. Chris Matthews, my District Outreach and Communications Director, passed away unexpectedly. If any one of you begin to lose faith in our country, remember Chris Matthews. Remember he was without question one of the Commonwealth’s sharpest political minds – a generational talent. Remember that he was more than a Congressional aide. He took the belief that through our actions we all can bring needed change and brought it with him on many interstate bus rides to canvas distant pivotal states and to the doors of the families he inspired. Remember through his example that public service is a genuinely noble vocation. As a trusted member of our office, he helped countless veterans, families, and those who could not advocate for themselves. Those of us privileged to have worked with him for over fifteen years will remember his laugh and his wry, often biting, humor – contrasting the way things are to the way they could be. We will always remember his authentic belief that in this country, people can bring about progress and meaningful change. It was real to him and his sincerity shown through. Chris was a genuinely good person. He was family to all of us, and we are devastated by his loss, particularly at such a young age. Our thoughts and prayers are with Molly and Eli and the many who loved him. Though we wish we had more time with him, his memory will continue to give us faith that one person can significantly make better the lives of those around him.

The Supreme Court’s decision today recognizes that states face unique circumstances in administering their elections. In Alaska, voting is not as simple as driving down the road to a neighborhood polling place. Many Alaskans live in remote communities that are not connected to the road system, requiring ballots to travel by bush plane or boat, which means volatile weather conditions and limited infrastructure can determine whether those ballots arrive on time. Even with Alaska’s current 10-day grace period for in-state ballots, we have seen mail delays cause legally cast ballots to arrive too late to be counted. Today’s decision affirms that states have the flexibility to account for these realities and helps ensure that every American who lawfully casts a ballot has the opportunity to have it counted. https://apnews.com/article/supreme-court-mailed-ballots-trump-elections-5f24f718ea92a33838485ce6302e079e

Salmon are integral to the Pacific Northwest's culture and ecosystems. The Select Area Fisheries Management (SAFE) program produces millions of hatchery fish each year, providing relief for endangered fish stocks and supporting Oregon’s commercial and recreational fishing industries.  The Bonneville Power Administration’s (BPA) recent decision to withdraw from the SAFE program puts all that at risk. Losing this critical funding will further risk salmon and steelhead stocks; limit commercial, Tribal, and recreational fishing in the region; and strain hatchery production. Oregon's environment and economy thrive when local fishing is reliable and sustainable. We’re calling for the BPA to fulfill its obligation, renew its contracts, and restore the SAFE program.

W000821.text: We are blessed to live in the greatest nation in the world. Happy Fourth of July and happy 250 years of independence, America!🇺🇸

Arkansas, and the United States, have an incredibly abundant source of timber. Unfortunately, we look to nations outside of our borders to supply us with a resource that we have right here in our own back yard. Healthy forest management is more than just taking care of our trees, in fact we have been loving our trees to death. Our forests are overstocked and unhealthy because we have no markets for the wood and rural communities are suffering because their resource and economic opportunity are tied directly to the forests. A nation with such an abundance of timber should never be reliant on other countries to import lumber and pulp products, but that’s where we find ourselves.  Recently, we’ve seen paper mills across the country closing – even a few here in the Fourth District. With a background in Forestry and Engineering, Congressman Westerman understands just how important our pulp and paper industry is and he remains heavily focused on legislation that will support such an important economic contributer for Arkansas. This week’s meeting with the Pulp & Paperworkers’ Resource Council to discuss just how important the forest products industry underscored the need for Congress to work diligently to provide its support.

S001198.text: Last week, at the Port of Alaska groundbreaking ceremony, I mentioned the pressure my team and I have put on federal agency heads to resolve a decade-long lawsuit over port funding. Yesterday, a settlement was finally announced, unlocking $191 million to go directly toward construction and building on the hundreds of millions of federal dollars my congressional delegation colleagues and I have secured for the project over the years. The funding we’ve secured for the port is critically important for Alaska, first, because it will lower the cost of living for Alaska’s hard-working families—everything from energy to groceries. The port modernization is also vital for supporting the renaissance of energy development happening on the North Slope and the future build-out of the Alaska LNG project. Finally, the Port of Alaska is very important to U.S. national security and the military build-up taking place in our state, especially the historic $7 billion ‘Fighter Town’ recapitalization coming to JBER. I will continue pressing for the funding needed to complete this project and bringing up top federal officials—like the U.S. Attorney General, the U.S. Transportation Secretary, the MARAD Administrator, and the USTRANSCOM Commander—so they understand and appreciate how important this piece of infrastructure is for Alaska and for America.

During my tenure in the Senate, I have worked to secure historic levels of federal infrastructure investments for Alaska—funding that will help improve roads, bridges, ports, airports, and other crucial projects to our great state. But funding alone does not build projects. Bridging the gap between federal funding and actual project delivery—getting projects designed, approved, bid on, and under construction so that Alaskans can get to work—is just as important as securing these investments.   Last week, I joined @USDOTFHWA Sean McMaster and union leaders representing thousands of Alaskans for a roundtable on delivering federally funded transportation projects, strengthening workforce development, expanding apprenticeship opportunities, and ensuring these investments create jobs for Alaskans and move projects forward.   I will always fight to ensure infrastructure investments in Alaska become a reality and benefit Alaskans.

A000375.text: John Adams called Independence Day America’s “Day of Deliverance.” The Declaration of Independence - that sacred parchment - is the cornerstone of American exceptionalism and the foundation for the longest-sustained constitutional democracy in the world. It affirms the birthright of every American citizen: our God-given rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. The Declaration of Independence wasn’t just a list of grievances; it was a treatise on man and his natural rights - a mission statement for how such men should be governed. No one at the time gave us a fighting chance of defeating the world’s superpower for our independence. And few predicted we’d persist for a quarter of a millennium. Our founding visionaries weren’t sure of either outcome themselves, but they believed in our inherent rights and God-given freedoms and would rather die fighting for them than live under tyranny. They trusted in “divine Providence” for protection and mutually pledged to each other “our Lives, our Fortunes and our sacred Honor.” They held fast to truth, they stood firm for justice, and they fought like warrior poets for our freedom. And, by the grace of Almighty God, our revolutionary ancestors gave birth to the most powerful and prosperous nation in human history. Let’s honor their vision, courage, and conviction by solemnly dedicating ourselves to preserving this “Great Experiment” in liberty and self-government. Happy 250th Independence Day to all my God-fearing, freedom-loving American patriots! May God continue to have mercy upon and give favor to our beloved nation. U-S-A, U-S-A…!! Your proud US Representative and fellow West Texan, Jodey

E000071.text: Today, 250 years ago, the world changed. America changed the course of human history. Over the last 250 years, America has endured war, hardship, division, and sacrifice. But we have also achieved the impossible, expanded freedom, inspired generations, and proven time and again that no challenge is too great when the American people stand together. The story of our nation has never been one of perfection. It has always been one of perseverance. Every generation has been called to leave this country stronger than they found it, and every generation has answered that call in its own way. On July 4, 1776, our Founding Fathers pledged their lives, fortunes, and sacred honor to establish a nation built on liberty and self-government. One year ago today, on the Fourth of July, our nation celebrated the blessings of freedom while families across Texas experienced unimaginable heartbreak. We pause today to remember every precious life lost at Camp Mystic and every other life taken far too soon in that tragedy. We remember the children whose futures were just beginning, the counselors and adults who stood courageously in harm’s way, and every family whose lives were forever changed. Their names, their stories, and their memories will never be forgotten. No words can truly ease the pain of such profound loss. Yet even in the darkest moments, we witnessed the very best of America. To every law enforcement officer, firefighter, EMS professional, dispatcher, game warden, pilot, medic, search-and-rescue specialist, and every first responder who answered the call, thank you. You ran toward danger while others were running away. You worked through exhaustion, heartbreak, and impossible conditions with courage, professionalism, and compassion. Your service honored every life you were fighting to save. To the countless volunteers who showed up without being asked—neighbors, veterans, church groups, ranchers, boat owners, businesses, families, and complete strangers—you reminded us that the strength of our communities is measured not only by what we say, but by what we do. You brought supplies, comfort, equipment, prayers, and hope. You asked for nothing in return except the opportunity to help another human being. That spirit defines Texas. As we remember those we lost, let us also remember the enduring responsibility we share: to love our neighbors, to care for those who grieve, and to ensure that the memories of these lives continue to inspire acts of kindness, service, and sacrifice. Finally, I want to offer my deepest gratitude to the men of the BEARKAT team. There are simply no words sufficient to express what you endured or what you accomplished. You answered a calling that demanded extraordinary courage, unwavering resolve, and selfless service. You carried burdens that few will ever fully understand, and you did so with quiet professionalism and humility. It is impossible to thank you enough for all that you did. Your actions brought comfort to grieving families, hope in moments of despair, and honor to everyone you represent. Texas will forever be grateful, and your service will never be forgotten. May we always remember those we lost, honor those who served, and carry forward the enduring truth that even in our darkest hours, courage, compassion, and faith will always light the way.

Colorado’s forced gray wolf reintroduction has left many ranchers in Western and Southern Colorado facing livestock losses, higher operating costs, and growing uncertainty about how to protect the animals their livelihoods depend on. The Pet and Livestock Protection Act recognizes what the science already shows: the gray wolf has recovered and exceeded federal recovery goals. The Endangered Species Act was designed to recover species, not keep them listed indefinitely. For the ranchers, outfitters, and rural communities I represent in #CO03, this is an affordability issue. Every livestock loss means higher costs, greater uncertainty, and real consequences for the families and businesses that help feed America. The recovery of the gray wolf is a conservation success. It’s time for federal policy to recognize that success while giving states the tools they need to responsibly manage wolf populations and protect rural livelihoods.

On this day in 1944, over 34,000 American soldiers crowded together in small, amphibious boats en route to Omaha Beach. As the boats landed on the beach, and their bow ramps dropped down leading the men ashore, unrelenting machine gun fire rained down from enemy bunkers. Undeterred, the American and Allied forces emerged from the battle victorious, but not without a heavy cost. Over 2,500 Americans died at Omaha Beach. As we remember the heroism Americans exhibited on D-Day and we reflect on the cost of freedom, may we remember and be inspired by the names and faces of those brave soldiers who died in service to our Country.

The Supreme Court has now issued its decision on birthright citizenship, resolving one of the most significant constitutional cases before the Court this term. I hope this provides a straightforward overview of the decision and its broader legal significance.

H001101.text: Hackers don't need to break today's encryption to steal today's data. They just need to steal it now, store it, and wait for a quantum computer powerful enough to crack it open later. Security experts call it "harvest now, decrypt later," and it's already happening to government systems. @POTUS saw this coming, which is why he signed Executive Order 14412 to get federal agencies moving toward quantum-resistant encryption. I introduced H.R. 9516 to codify that order into law, so the shift doesn't stall out or get undone by a future administration. Some fights shouldn't depend on who's in the White House, and this is one of them.

Somewhere in this country, a young American family is doing everything right. They got married. They saved. They worked overtime, cut expenses, and put money aside every month with one goal in mind: buying their first home and building something lasting for their kids. The average first-time homebuyer in America is now 40 years old, a record high. Home prices relative to income have nearly doubled since 1976. That young family playing by the rules is getting crushed, and Washington has spent years telling them it’s complicated. It’s not complicated. A new Federal Reserve study found that illegal immigration was responsible for 30% of home price growth and 20% of rent growth between 2021 and 2024. Biden flooded this country with millions of illegal aliens, every one of them competed for the same finite housing stock that young family was saving for, and Washington subsidized it the entire time with taxpayer-backed mortgage loans that were never meant for noncitizens. That family deserves better. My Homeownership Eligibility Reform Act restricts taxpayer-backed mortgages to U.S. citizens only, permanently. No future administration can reverse it with the stroke of a pen, and no young American family gets priced out of their dream because Washington decided illegal aliens come first. I’m fighting back.
